import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# In parallelohedron

The Voronoi conjecture asks whether every convex polytope that tiles Euclidean space by
translations is affinely equivalent to the Dirichlet–Voronoi cell of a lattice. The conjecture
is known in dimensions at most five and is open in higher dimensions.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Parallelohedron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/parallelohedron)
- [Garber, *Voronoi conjecture for five-dimensional parallelohedra*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.05193)
-/

namespace InParallelohedron

/-- A full-dimensional convex polytope in `ℝ^d`, represented as the convex hull of finitely many
points and required to have nonempty interior. -/
def IsFullDimensionalConvexPolytope {d : ℕ} (P : Set (Fin d → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  (interior P).Nonempty ∧ ∃ V : Finset (Fin d → ℝ), convexHull ℝ (V : Set (Fin d → ℝ)) = P

/-- A set `P` tiles `ℝ^d` by translations if some family of its translates covers the whole
space and distinct translates have disjoint interiors. -/
def TilesByTranslation {d : ℕ} (P : Set (Fin d → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : Set (Fin d → ℝ),
    (⋃ t ∈ T, translateSet P t) = Set.univ ∧
      ∀ ⦃t₁ t₂⦄, t₁ ∈ T → t₂ ∈ T → t₁ ≠ t₂ →
        Disjoint (interior (translateSet P t₁)) (interior (translateSet P t₂))

/-- A full-rank lattice in `ℝ^d` is a discrete `ℤ`-submodule whose real span is the whole
space. -/
def IsFullRankLattice {d : ℕ} (Λ : Submodule ℤ (Fin d → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  DiscreteTopology Λ ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (Λ : Set (Fin d → ℝ)) = ⊤

/-- The closed Dirichlet–Voronoi cell at the origin of a lattice `Λ`: the points at least as
close to `0` as to every lattice point. -/
def dirichletVoronoiCell {d : ℕ} (Λ : Submodule ℤ (Fin d → ℝ)) : Set (Fin d → ℝ) :=
  {x | ∀ y ∈ (Λ : Set (Fin d → ℝ)), dist x 0 ≤ dist x y}

/--
**Voronoi's conjecture.** In every dimension `d`, every full-dimensional convex `d`-polytope `P`
that tiles `ℝ^d` by translations is carried by an invertible affine transformation to the
Dirichlet–Voronoi cell of some full-rank lattice in `ℝ^d`. Delaunay proved the result through
dimension four, and the five-dimensional case is also known; the higher-dimensional cases remain
open.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem parts.ii (d : ℕ) (P : Set (Fin d → ℝ))
    (hP : IsFullDimensionalConvexPolytope P) (hTile : TilesByTranslation P) :
    ∃ (Λ : Submodule ℤ (Fin d → ℝ)) (A : (Fin d → ℝ) ≃ᵃ[ℝ] (Fin d → ℝ)),
      IsFullRankLattice Λ ∧ A '' P = dirichletVoronoiCell Λ := by
  sorry

end InParallelohedron
modeling_decisions: The bare list heading was interpreted using the linked parallelohedron article and the cited precise formulation in arXiv:1906.05193.

Part (ii) states Voronoi's conjecture in every dimension, as in the cited precise formulation; the docstring records that dimensions at most five are known and the higher-dimensional cases remain open.
Euclidean d-space is modeled as `Fin d → ℝ`. A convex d-polytope is required to be a finite convex hull with nonempty ambient interior, making full-dimensionality explicit.

A translational tiling is modeled by exact coverage by translates and pairwise disjoint interiors of distinct translates. No face-to-face hypothesis is imposed, since the conjecture concerns the tile and the source notes that a face-to-face lattice tiling may be assumed without loss.
An affine transformation is modeled by an `AffineEquiv`, so it is invertible as intended.

A lattice is modeled as a discrete `ℤ`-submodule whose real span is the whole ambient space. Its Dirichlet–Voronoi cell is centered at the lattice point zero; choosing zero loses no generality for a lattice.
Part (i) was not replaced by a planar graph or face-adjacency statement, because the decomposition explicitly requires the incidence structure of patches to agree with a full Fedorov face lattice.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# In parallelohedron

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Parallelohedron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/parallelohedron)
- [Garber, Magazinov, *Voronoi conjecture for five-dimensional
  parallelohedra*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.05193)
-/

namespace InParallelohedron

open Set Module

/-- A full-dimensional polytope is the convex hull of finitely many points and has nonempty
interior. -/
def IsFullDimensionalPolytope {d : ℕ} (P : Set (Fin d → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  (∃ V : Finset (Fin d → ℝ), convexHull ℝ (V : Set (Fin d → ℝ)) = P) ∧
    (interior P).Nonempty

/-- The translates of `P` indexed by `T` cover space and have pairwise disjoint interiors. -/
def TilesByTranslations {d : ℕ} (P : Set (Fin d → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : Set (Fin d → ℝ),
    (⋃ t ∈ T, {x | x - t ∈ P}) = Set.univ ∧
    ∀ ⦃t₁⦄, t₁ ∈ T → ∀ ⦃t₂⦄, t₂ ∈ T → t₁ ≠ t₂ →
      Disjoint {x | x - t₁ ∈ interior P} {x | x - t₂ ∈ interior P}

/-- A planar polygonal disk in three-dimensional space. Allowing a finite union of convex
polygons includes concave faces. -/
def IsPlanarPolygon (F : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  (∃ pieces : Set (Set (Fin 3 → ℝ)), pieces.Finite ∧
    (∀ p ∈ pieces, ∃ V : Finset (Fin 3 → ℝ), convexHull ℝ (V : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ)) = p) ∧
    (⋃ p ∈ pieces, p) = F) ∧
  Module.finrank ℝ (affineSpan ℝ F).direction = 2 ∧
  Nonempty ((Metric.closedBall (0 : Fin 2 → ℝ) 1 : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ)) ≃ₜ F)

/-- A finite polygonal face decomposition of the spherical boundary of a solid polyhedron.
Distinct faces can meet only in a vertex or a full nondegenerate edge, and adjacent faces are
not coplanar, so the decomposition does not artificially subdivide a face. -/
def IsPolyhedralSphere (P : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ)) (faces : Set (Set (Fin 3 → ℝ))) : Prop :=
  faces.Finite ∧
  (interior P).Nonempty ∧ closure (interior P) = P ∧
  (⋃ F ∈ faces, F) = frontier P ∧
  Nonempty ((Metric.sphere (0 : Fin 3 → ℝ) 1 : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ)) ≃ₜ frontier P) ∧
  (∀ F ∈ faces, IsPlanarPolygon F) ∧
  ∀ F ∈ faces, ∀ G ∈ faces, F ≠ G →
    (F ∩ G = ∅ ∨ (∃ x, F ∩ G = {x}) ∨
      ∃ x y, x ≠ y ∧ F ∩ G = convexHull ℝ ({x, y} : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ))) ∧
    ((∃ x y, x ≠ y ∧ F ∩ G = convexHull ℝ ({x, y} : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ))) →
      affineSpan ℝ F ≠ affineSpan ℝ G)

/-- Two faces in a polygonal boundary decomposition are adjacent when their intersection is a
nondegenerate edge. -/
def FaceAdjacent (F G : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ x y, x ≠ y ∧ F ∩ G = convexHull ℝ ({x, y} : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ))

/-- A set of faces is connected through shared edges. -/
def FacesConnected {faces : Set (Set (Fin 3 → ℝ))} (C : Set faces) : Prop :=
  C.Nonempty ∧ ∀ F ∈ C, ∀ G ∈ C,
    Relation.ReflTransGen (fun A B : faces => FaceAdjacent A.1 B.1 ∧ A ∈ C ∧ B ∈ C) F G

/-- The geometric regions obtained by taking the unions of all faces in each patch. -/
def PatchRegions {faces : Set (Set (Fin 3 → ℝ))} (patches : Set (Set faces)) :
    Set (Set (Fin 3 → ℝ)) :=
  {R | ∃ C ∈ patches, R = ⋃ F ∈ C, F.1}

/-- The incidence cells generated by a collection of closed regions. Intersecting with the union
of all regions makes the intersection of the empty subcollection the top cell. -/
def IncidenceCells (regions : Set (Set (Fin 3 → ℝ))) : Set (Set (Fin 3 → ℝ)) :=
  {X | ∃ S : Set regions, X = (⋃ R ∈ regions, R) ∩ ⋂ R ∈ S, R.1}

/-- A grouping of the faces has the combinatorics of the model's faces when it is a partition into
edge-connected patches and the inclusion posets of all incidence cells generated by the patches
and by the model faces are isomorphic. -/
def IsFedorovPatching (faces modelFaces : Set (Set (Fin 3 → ℝ))) : Prop :=
  ∃ patches : Set (Set faces),
    Setoid.IsPartition patches ∧
    (∀ C ∈ patches, FacesConnected C) ∧
    ∃ e : IncidenceCells (PatchRegions patches) ≃ IncidenceCells modelFaces,
      ∀ X Y, (X.1 ⊆ Y.1) ↔ (e X).1 ⊆ (e Y).1

/-- **Grünbaum's conjecture.** Every (not necessarily convex) solid polyhedron whose boundary is
topologically a sphere and which tiles three-dimensional space by translations admits a grouping
of its faces into connected patches. The patch incidence structure is that of the faces of one of
Fedorov's five parallelohedra (a parallelepiped, hexagonal prism, rhombic dodecahedron, elongated
dodecahedron, or truncated octahedron). -/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem in_parallelohedron.parts.i :
    ∀ (P : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ)) (faces : Set (Set (Fin 3 → ℝ))),
      IsPolyhedralSphere P faces → TilesByTranslations P →
      ∃ (Q : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ)) (modelFaces : Set (Set (Fin 3 → ℝ))),
        IsFullDimensionalPolytope Q ∧ IsPolyhedralSphere Q modelFaces ∧
          TilesByTranslations Q ∧ IsFedorovPatching faces modelFaces := by
  sorry

/-- The Dirichlet–Voronoi cell at the origin of `L`. -/
def dirichletVoronoiCell {d : ℕ} (L : Submodule ℤ (Fin d → ℝ)) : Set (Fin d → ℝ) :=
  {x | ∀ v, v ∈ L → dist x 0 ≤ dist x v}

/-- **Voronoi's conjecture.** In every dimension, every full-dimensional convex polytope which
tiles Euclidean space by translations is affinely equivalent to the Dirichlet–Voronoi cell of a
full-rank lattice. The result is known through dimension five and remains open in dimensions six
and higher. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 51 52]
theorem in_parallelohedron.parts.ii :
    ∀ (d : ℕ) (P : Set (Fin d → ℝ)), IsFullDimensionalPolytope P → TilesByTranslations P →
      ∃ (b : Basis (Fin d) ℝ (Fin d → ℝ)) (L : Submodule ℤ (Fin d → ℝ))
          (A : (Fin d → ℝ) ≃ᵃ[ℝ] (Fin d → ℝ)),
        L = Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range b) ∧ A '' P = dirichletVoronoiCell L := by
  sorry

end InParallelohedron
modeling_decisions: For Grünbaum's conjecture, a polyhedron is modeled as a regular closed solid in ℝ³ together with a finite polygonal-disk decomposition of its boundary; the boundary is explicitly homeomorphic to the unit 2-sphere. Faces may be concave, since a polygonal disk is allowed to be a finite union of convex polygons.

Translational tiling means exact coverage by translates with pairwise disjoint translated interiors. This is the closed-polytope version of tiling, rather than the measure-almost-everywhere predicate used by the repository's spectral-set API.
A patch is a part of a genuine partition of the face set and is connected through shared nondegenerate edges. Its geometric region is the union of its constituent faces.

The full combinatorial incidence structure is represented by the inclusion poset of cells obtained from intersections of patch regions. An inclusion-preserving equivalence with the analogous poset generated by the model facets expresses equality of face lattices.

The model in part i is quantified as an arbitrary full-dimensional convex translational tile in ℝ³. By Fedorov's established three-dimensional classification, these are exactly the five listed combinatorial types, so this avoids choosing coordinates for five representatives without broadening the mathematical class.

For part ii, a full-dimensional polytope is a finite convex hull with nonempty interior. A full-rank lattice is represented explicitly as the integer span of a real basis, and the Dirichlet–Voronoi cell is centered at the lattice origin.

Part ii is stated uniformly for every natural-number dimension, including dimension zero. The zero-dimensional instance has the expected singleton polytope, zero lattice, and singleton Voronoi cell and does not alter the higher-dimensional conjecture.

finitely many points. -/

  ∃ V : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)),
    V.Finite ∧ P = convexHull ℝ V ∧ affineSpan ℝ P = ⊤

space and distinct translates have disjoint interiors. -/

  ∃ T : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)),
    (⋃ v ∈ T, {x | x - v ∈ P}) = Set.univ ∧
      T.Pairwise fun v w ↦
        Disjoint (interior {x | x - v ∈ P}) (interior {x | x - w ∈ P})

/-- The Dirichlet–Voronoi cell at the origin of a subgroup `L` of Euclidean space. -/
def dirichletVoronoiCell {d : ℕ} (L : Submodule ℤ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) :
    Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :=
  {x | ∀ l : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), l ∈ L → dist x 0 ≤ dist x l}

/--
**Voronoi conjecture.** For every positive dimension $d$ and every convex $d$-polytope $P$
that tiles $\mathbb{R}^d$ by translations, there are a full lattice $\Lambda$ and an affine
transformation $A$ such that $A(P)$ is the Dirichlet–Voronoi cell of $\Lambda$. The conjecture is
known for $d \leq 5$ and remains open in higher dimensions.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem in_parallelohedron.parts.ii :
    ∀ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d → ∀ P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)),
      IsFullDimensionalPolytope P → TilesByTranslations P →
        ∃ (L : Submodule ℤ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)))
          (A : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) ≃ᵃ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)),
          IsDiscrete (L : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) ∧
            Submodule.span ℝ (L : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) = ⊤ ∧
              A '' P = dirichletVoronoiCell L := by
  sorry

end InParallelohedron

A d-dimensional polytope in ℝ^d is represented as the convex hull of a finite vertex set whose affine span is the whole ambient Euclidean space. Convexity is therefore built into the definition and lower-dimensional degeneracies are excluded.

Tiling by translations is modeled in the standard closed-tile sense: a set of translates covers the whole space, and interiors of distinct translates are disjoint. No face-to-face condition is imposed, in accordance with the source and decomposition note.

A full lattice is represented by a ℤ-submodule that is discrete as a subset of Euclidean space and whose real span is the whole space. Finite generation alone was deliberately not used because it does not imply discreteness for ℤ-submodules of a real vector space.

The Dirichlet–Voronoi cell is centered at the lattice origin and uses non-strict distance inequalities against every lattice point. Allowing an arbitrary affine equivalence, including translation, matches the source formulation.
Dimensions are quantified as natural numbers with d ≥ 1, reflecting the standard positive-dimensional scope of parallelohedra; the known d ≤ 5 cases remain included in the universal conjecture.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# In parallelohedron

A *parallelohedron* is a convex polyhedron whose translated copies tile $\mathbb{R}^3$; its
higher-dimensional analogues (convex polytopes tiling $\mathbb{R}^d$ by translations) are called
*parallelotopes* or $d$-dimensional parallelohedra. The Dirichlet–Voronoi cell of a lattice is
always a parallelohedron. The **Voronoi conjecture** asserts the converse up to affine
transformations: every $d$-dimensional parallelohedron is an affine image of the Dirichlet–Voronoi
cell of some $d$-dimensional lattice. Delone (1929) proved this for $d \le 4$ and Garber (2019)
for $d = 5$; it is open for $d \ge 6$.

*References:*
- [Parallelohedron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/parallelohedron)
- [List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Voronoi conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voronoi_conjecture)
- A. Garber, *Voronoi conjecture for five-dimensional parallelohedra*,
  [arXiv:1906.05193](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.05193)
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry Pointwise

namespace InParallelohedron

/-- A set `P ⊆ ℝ^d` **tiles `ℝ^d` by translations** if there is a set `T` of translation vectors
such that the translates `t +ᵥ P` (`t ∈ T`) cover `ℝ^d` and have pairwise disjoint interiors. -/
def TilesByTranslation {d : ℕ} (P : Set (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : Set (ℝ^d), (⋃ t ∈ T, t +ᵥ P) = Set.univ ∧
    T.Pairwise fun t₁ t₂ => Disjoint (interior (t₁ +ᵥ P)) (interior (t₂ +ᵥ P))

/-- The **Dirichlet–Voronoi cell** of a set `Λ ⊆ ℝ^d` (around the origin): the set of points that
are at least as close to `0` as to any point of `Λ`. When `Λ` is a lattice, this is the
Dirichlet–Voronoi polytope of the lattice. -/
def voronoiCell {d : ℕ} (Λ : Set (ℝ^d)) : Set (ℝ^d) :=
  {x | ∀ y ∈ Λ, dist x 0 ≤ dist x y}

/-- The whole space tiles itself by translations. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem tilesByTranslation_univ (d : ℕ) : TilesByTranslation (Set.univ : Set (ℝ^d)) :=
  ⟨{0}, by simp, Set.pairwise_singleton _ _⟩

/-- The origin lies in every Dirichlet–Voronoi cell. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem zero_mem_voronoiCell {d : ℕ} (Λ : Set (ℝ^d)) : (0 : ℝ^d) ∈ voronoiCell Λ :=
  fun _ _ => by simp

/-- **Voronoi conjecture.** Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a convex $d$-dimensional polytope
(the convex hull of a finite set, with nonempty interior) that tiles $\mathbb{R}^d$ by translations,
i.e. a $d$-dimensional parallelohedron. Then there exist a lattice $\Lambda \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$
and an affine transformation $\mathcal{A}$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$ such that $\mathcal{A}(P)$ is the
Dirichlet–Voronoi cell of $\Lambda$. In the words of the Wikipedia article: every parallelohedron
can be made into a plesiohedron (a Dirichlet–Voronoi cell of a lattice) by an affine
transformation.

This is known for $d \le 5$ (Delone for $d \le 4$, Garber for $d = 5$) and open for $d \ge 6$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem in_parallelohedron.parts.ii (d : ℕ) (S : Finset (ℝ^d))
    (h_int : (interior (convexHull ℝ (S : Set (ℝ^d)))).Nonempty)
    (h_tile : TilesByTranslation (convexHull ℝ (S : Set (ℝ^d)))) :
    ∃ (Λ : Submodule ℤ (ℝ^d)) (_ : DiscreteTopology Λ) (_ : IsZLattice ℝ Λ)
      (A : ℝ^d ≃ᵃ[ℝ] ℝ^d), A '' convexHull ℝ (S : Set (ℝ^d)) = voronoiCell (Λ : Set (ℝ^d)) := by
  sorry

/-- The Voronoi conjecture holds in dimension at most five: Delone proved it for $d \le 4$
(1929) and Garber proved it for $d = 5$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem in_parallelohedron.parts.ii.variants.dim_le_five (d : ℕ) (hd : d ≤ 5) (S : Finset (ℝ^d))
    (h_int : (interior (convexHull ℝ (S : Set (ℝ^d)))).Nonempty)
    (h_tile : TilesByTranslation (convexHull ℝ (S : Set (ℝ^d)))) :
    ∃ (Λ : Submodule ℤ (ℝ^d)) (_ : DiscreteTopology Λ) (_ : IsZLattice ℝ Λ)
      (A : ℝ^d ≃ᵃ[ℝ] ℝ^d), A '' convexHull ℝ (S : Set (ℝ^d)) = voronoiCell (Λ : Set (ℝ^d)) := by
  sorry

end InParallelohedron

/-!
# In parallelohedron

A *parallelohedron* (in dimension $3$) or *parallelotope* (in general dimension $d$) is a
convex polytope in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose translated copies tile $\mathbb{R}^d$. Voronoi cells
of lattices are parallelohedra, and the **Voronoi conjecture** asserts the converse up to
affine transformations: every parallelohedron is an affine image of the Dirichlet–Voronoi
polytope of some lattice. Delaunay proved this for $d \le 4$ (the cases $d \le 3$ being
folklore), Garber proved it for $d = 5$, and it is open for $d \ge 6$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Parallelohedron*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/parallelohedron)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [A. Garber, *Voronoi conjecture for five-dimensional parallelohedra*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.05193)
-/

namespace InParallelohedron

open scoped Pointwise

variable {d : ℕ}

/-- A set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ **tiles $\mathbb{R}^d$ by translations** if there is a set
$T$ of translation vectors such that the translates $t + P$, $t \in T$, cover $\mathbb{R}^d$ and
any two distinct translates have disjoint interiors. -/
def TilesByTranslations (P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)),
    (⋃ t ∈ T, t +ᵥ P) = Set.univ ∧
    T.Pairwise fun s t => Disjoint (interior (s +ᵥ P)) (interior (t +ᵥ P))

/-- A **$d$-dimensional parallelohedron** is a convex $d$-polytope in $\mathbb{R}^d$, i.e. the
convex hull of a finite set with nonempty interior, that tiles $\mathbb{R}^d$ by translations.
Requiring a nonempty interior excludes lower-dimensional convex hulls, whose translates can
trivially cover $\mathbb{R}^d$ with (empty) pairwise disjoint interiors. -/
def IsParallelohedron (P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) : Prop :=
  (∃ S : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), P = convexHull ℝ ↑S) ∧
    (interior P).Nonempty ∧ TilesByTranslations P

/-- The (closed) **Dirichlet–Voronoi cell** of the origin with respect to a set
$\Lambda \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$: the set of points that are at least as close to $0$ as to any
point of $\Lambda$. When $\Lambda$ is a lattice this is the Dirichlet–Voronoi polytope of
$\Lambda$. -/
def voronoiCell (Λ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :=
  {x | ∀ v ∈ Λ, dist x 0 ≤ dist x v}

/-- The origin lies in every Dirichlet–Voronoi cell of the origin. -/
@[category API]
theorem zero_mem_voronoiCell (Λ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) : 0 ∈ voronoiCell Λ :=
  fun v _ => by simp

/-- The Dirichlet–Voronoi cell with respect to the empty set is the whole space. -/
@[category API]
theorem voronoiCell_empty : voronoiCell (∅ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) = Set.univ := by
  ext x
  simp [voronoiCell]

/-- **Voronoi's conjecture** (the open part of the parallelohedron problem).

Every parallelohedron can be made into a plesiohedron (the Voronoi cell of a lattice) by an
affine transformation. Precisely: for every $d$ and every convex $d$-polytope $P$ that tiles
$\mathbb{R}^d$ by translations, there exist a lattice $\Lambda \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ (the
$\mathbb{Z}$-span of a basis $b$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$) and an affine transformation $\mathcal{A}$ of
$\mathbb{R}^d$ such that $\mathcal{A}(P)$ is the Dirichlet–Voronoi polytope of $\Lambda$.

Delaunay (1929) proved this for $d \le 4$ (in particular for the three-dimensional
parallelohedra), Garber proved it for $d = 5$, and it remains open for $d \ge 6$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem in_parallelohedron.parts.ii :
    ∀ (d : ℕ) (P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))), IsParallelohedron P →
      ∃ (b : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)))
        (A : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) ≃ᵃ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)),
        A '' P = voronoiCell (Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range b)) := by
  sorry

end InParallelohedron

The conjecture is stated for all dimensions d (as Voronoi stated it), not only for the open range d ≥ 6; the file tags it research open because the general statement is open.

'Parallelohedron' = convex hull of a finite set of points of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) with nonempty interior that tiles ℝ^d by translations (some family of translates covers ℝ^d and distinct translates have disjoint interiors). Face-to-face or lattice structure of the tiling is NOT assumed, matching Garber's definition (Venkov/McMullen show these are automatic). The nonempty-interior hypothesis is needed: lower-dimensional convex hulls would otherwise 'tile' via uncountably many translates with empty interiors, making the statement false.

A lattice is modeled concretely as Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range b) for an ℝ-basis b : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), exactly Garber's definition ('integer linear combinations of some basis'); Mathlib provides the IsZLattice instance for this, so it agrees with Mathlib's lattice notion. WLOG the lattice contains 0 and the cell of 0 is taken, since translations are affine.
The Dirichlet–Voronoi polytope is the CLOSED cell {x | ∀ v ∈ Λ, dist x 0 ≤ dist x v} (the standard compact polytope), rather than the open cell of strictly closer points.

An affine transformation is an affine equivalence E ≃ᵃ[ℝ] E; this is equivalent to using an arbitrary affine map, since any affine map sending a full-dimensional body onto a full-dimensional body is bijective.
AMS tags 51 52 chosen to match the problem tags (geometry / Euclidean geometry) and the subject (convex and discrete geometry, tilings).

The d = 0 instance is trivially true (a point tiles the zero space and equals the Voronoi cell of the trivial lattice); no lower bound on d was imposed since the source states the conjecture for every d.

higher-dimensional Voronoi conjecture for parallelohedra.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Parallelohedron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/parallelohedron)

namespace InParallelohedron

/-- The translate of `P` by the vector `t`. -/
def translate {d : ℕ} (P : Set (Fin d → ℝ)) (t : Fin d → ℝ) : Set (Fin d → ℝ) :=
  {x | x - t ∈ P}

/-- A set tiles Euclidean space by translations if some family of its translates covers the
space and distinct translates have disjoint interiors. -/
def TilesByTranslation {d : ℕ} (P : Set (Fin d → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : Set (Fin d → ℝ),
    (⋃ t ∈ T, translate P t) = Set.univ ∧
      T.Pairwise fun t u ↦ Disjoint (interior (translate P t)) (interior (translate P u))

/-- A full-dimensional convex polytope is the convex hull of finitely many points and has full
affine span. -/
def IsFullDimensionalConvexPolytope {d : ℕ} (P : Set (Fin d → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  (∃ v : Set (Fin d → ℝ), v.Finite ∧ P = convexHull ℝ v) ∧ affineSpan ℝ P = ⊤

/-- A polygonal region in three-space. -/
def IsPolygon (F : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ v : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ), v.Finite ∧ F = convexHull ℝ v ∧
    Module.finrank ℝ (affineSpan ℝ v).direction = 2

/-- Data describing a possibly nonconvex polyhedron whose boundary is a polygonal two-sphere. -/
structure PolyhedralSphere where
  /-- The closed solid bounded by the polyhedral surface. -/
  solid : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ)
  /-- The two-dimensional faces in the boundary decomposition. -/
  faces : Set (Set (Fin 3 → ℝ))
  faces_finite : faces.Finite
  solid_bounded : Bornology.IsBounded solid
  solid_regular : closure (interior solid) = solid
  face_polygon : ∀ F ∈ faces, IsPolygon F
  face_intersections : ∀ F ∈ faces, ∀ G ∈ faces, F ≠ G →
    (F ∩ G).Nonempty → Module.finrank ℝ (affineSpan ℝ (F ∩ G)).direction ≤ 1
  boundary_eq : frontier solid = ⋃₀ faces
  boundary_sphere : Nonempty
    (↥(frontier solid) ≃ₜ ↥(Metric.sphere (0 : Fin 3 → ℝ) 1))

/-- The facets of a convex set, defined intrinsically as its maximal proper faces. -/
def facets {d : ℕ} (P : Set (Fin d → ℝ)) : Set (Set (Fin d → ℝ)) :=
  {F | F.Nonempty ∧ F ⊆ P ∧ F ≠ P ∧ Convex ℝ F ∧
    (∀ x ∈ P, ∀ y ∈ P, (openSegment ℝ x y ∩ F).Nonempty → x ∈ F ∧ y ∈ F) ∧
    ∀ G : Set (Fin d → ℝ), G.Nonempty → G ⊆ P → G ≠ P → Convex ℝ G →
      (∀ x ∈ P, ∀ y ∈ P, (openSegment ℝ x y ∩ G).Nonempty → x ∈ G ∧ y ∈ G) →
      F ⊆ G → F = G}

/-- Replace each collection of faces in a patching by its geometric union. -/
def patchRegions (patches : Set (Set (Set (Fin 3 → ℝ)))) : Set (Set (Fin 3 → ℝ)) :=
  (fun p ↦ ⋃₀ p) '' patches

/-- The incidence poset generated by a family of regions: its elements are all nonempty
intersections of nonempty subfamilies, ordered by inclusion. -/
def intersectionPoset {α : Type*} (C : Set (Set α)) : Set (Set α) :=
  {r | ∃ D : Set (Set α), D.Nonempty ∧ D ⊆ C ∧ r = ⋂₀ D ∧ r.Nonempty}

/-- Grünbaum's conjecture: if a polyhedron has boundary topologically a sphere and its solid
can tile `ℝ³` by translations, then its faces can be partitioned into connected patches whose
incidence structure is that of the facets of one of the five Fedorov parallelohedra
(parallelepiped, hexagonal prism, rhombic dodecahedron, elongated dodecahedron, or truncated
octahedron). Here the target is expressed as a convex three-dimensional translational tile;
Fedorov's classification says these are precisely the five listed combinatorial types. -/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem parts.i :
    ∀ S : PolyhedralSphere, TilesByTranslation S.solid →
      ∃ patches : Set (Set (Set (Fin 3 → ℝ))),
        patches.Finite ∧ (∀ p ∈ patches, p.Nonempty ∧ p ⊆ S.faces ∧ IsConnected (⋃₀ p)) ∧
        ⋃₀ patches = S.faces ∧ Set.PairwiseDisjoint patches id ∧
        ∃ Q : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ), IsFullDimensionalConvexPolytope Q ∧ TilesByTranslation Q ∧
          Nonempty (↥(intersectionPoset (patchRegions patches)) ≃o
            ↥(intersectionPoset (facets Q))) := by
  sorry

/-- The image of the standard integer lattice under an invertible real linear map. -/
def IsLattice {d : ℕ} (Λ : Set (Fin d → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : (Fin d → ℝ) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (Fin d → ℝ),
    Λ = A '' {x | ∀ i, ∃ z : ℤ, x i = (z : ℝ)}

/-- The Dirichlet–Voronoi cell at the origin of a subset of Euclidean space. -/
def dirichletVoronoiCell {d : ℕ} (Λ : Set (Fin d → ℝ)) : Set (Fin d → ℝ) :=
  {x | ∀ l ∈ Λ, dist x 0 ≤ dist x l}

/-- The Voronoi conjecture: for every `d`, every full-dimensional convex `d`-polytope that
tiles `ℝᵈ` by translations is carried by an affine automorphism to the Dirichlet–Voronoi cell
of a lattice. The conjecture is known in dimensions at most five and remains open in higher
dimensions. -/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem parts.ii :
    ∀ d : ℕ, ∀ P : Set (Fin d → ℝ),
      IsFullDimensionalConvexPolytope P → TilesByTranslation P →
        ∃ Λ : Set (Fin d → ℝ), ∃ A : (Fin d → ℝ) ≃ᵃ[ℝ] (Fin d → ℝ),
          IsLattice Λ ∧ A '' P = dirichletVoronoiCell Λ := by
  sorry

end InParallelohedron
modeling_decisions: The terse list entry was expanded using the supplied Wikipedia parallelohedron article and, for the Voronoi conjecture, arXiv:1906.05193.

Ordinary translational tiling is modeled by exact set-theoretic coverage by translates and pairwise disjoint interiors. This permits the intended boundary intersections and avoids weakening a geometric tiling to almost-everywhere coverage.

A possibly nonconvex three-dimensional polyhedron is modeled by a bounded regular closed solid with a finite decomposition of its frontier into two-dimensional convex polygons; distinct polygons meet only in affine dimension at most one, and the frontier is homeomorphic to the unit 2-sphere.
A patch is a nonempty subset of the face family whose geometric union is connected. The patches form a pairwise-disjoint cover of the face family, hence a partition.

Combinatorial incidence is modeled by the inclusion order on all nonempty intersections of nonempty families of patch regions (and likewise of target facets). This captures facets, edges, vertices, and their incidence while omitting the empty and top elements on both sides.

Instead of hard-coding coordinate models for the five Fedorov types, the target in part (i) is a full-dimensional convex three-polytope tiling space by translations. Fedorov's classification identifies exactly five combinatorial types of such targets, so this expresses 'one of the five' without choosing special metric representatives.
A convex d-polytope is represented as the convex hull of a finite set with full affine span. The full-span condition makes the source's phrase 'd-polytope' explicit.

A lattice in ℝ^d is the image of the standard integer lattice under an invertible real linear map. Its Dirichlet–Voronoi cell is centered at zero, which is harmless because every such lattice contains zero and the conjecture allows an affine transformation.

Part (ii) states the canonical universal Voronoi conjecture for every natural-number dimension, as in the primary source and decomposition notes. The docstring records that dimensions at most five are known and only higher dimensions remain open.
